newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbek government presents 1997 investment programm.
newsitem.headline: Uzbek government presents 1997 investment programm.

text.p: Uzbekistan's government has approved an investment programme for the current year aiming to boost total investment in the economy to 301.6 billion sum from 166.5 billion last year.

Under a government decision made public on Wednesday, foreign investment will amount to $1.9 billion this year, including $1.3 billion guaranteed by the government, and $601 million of direct investment.
Total foreign investment in the Uzbek economy was $825 million last year.
The government says that foreign investors have pledged to invest in the Central Asian state's key sectors a total of $4.97 billion, including $3.8 billion guaranteed by the government.

Foreigners are expected to invest in the next few years a total of $869 million in the oil and gas sector, $537 million in mining, $402 million in air transport, $341 million in the chemical industry and $219 in telecommunications.

The government has selected 48 investment projects it would hold under its tight control. These include the Shurtan oil and gas complex, the Bukhara oil refinery, the Amantaitau Goldfields joint venture, the reconstruction of the Fergana oil refinery and the Navoi metallurgical plant.
Despite foreign investment commitments, the bulk of investment is expected to be made by the state and local companies.
Official projections for a rapid investment rise this year are based on the official exchange rate of some 60 Uzbek sums to the dollar, while the real market rate is at least 120 sums per dollar.
